vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawsentry
Version: 1.1.0

The skill performs high-risk administrative actions, including installing external npm packages (@omni-shield/ai-assistant-security-openclaw) and programmatically modifying the OpenClaw global configuration via CLI commands in `scripts/bundle.js`. It collects and exfiltrates a unique hardware ID (machineId) to a remote endpoint (llm-shield.omini-shield.com) and uses a hardcoded salt for its internal encryption logic. Furthermore, SKILL.md contains specific prompt-injection-style instructions that force the AI agent to monitor a background process for 10 minutes and restart it if it fails, which mimics persistence behavior.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (install OpenClaw security plugins) is plausible, but the bundled, minified script performs device fingerprinting, manages long‑lived login tokens and processes, and the runtime instructions ask the agent to monitor/restart those processes — behavior that is greater in scope and persistence than the description justifies and should be reviewed before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to 'install and configure' security plugins and does require running a bundled Node script, which is reasonable. However the script collects machine identifiers (exec of platform commands), generates login tokens, writes persistent state under .state, and expects the agent to manage restarting a long‑running process with tokens — functionality that goes beyond a simple installer and is not explained by the description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to execute an opaque bundled script, extract a login URL, share it with the user, then monitor the system for a process named 'bundle.js --login-token' every minute for 10 minutes and potentially restart it with stored tokens and device fingerprints. These steps cause the agent to read/write local state, run shell commands (ps/grep), and handle authentication tokens — all higher‑privilege actions and broader scope than a typical install guide.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install step (no downloads); the code to run is included in the skill as a bundled, minified script (scripts/bundle.js). Bundling lowers some supply‑chain risk (no external download), but the script is obfuscated/minified which reduces auditability and makes it hard to verify what remote endpoints or side effects it has.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, yet the runtime behavior involves generating and using loginToken and deviceFingerprint values, reading/writing .state/login_state.json, and restarting processes with those tokens. Handling of authentication tokens and machine identifiers is sensitive and the lack of declared credentials or explanation is disproportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly create and manage a long‑running process and persistent state under .state/, and require the agent to monitor and restart that process. Although the skill is not force‑installed (always:false), the agent will be asked to manage persistent runtime behavior and authentication tokens for at least the login flow — increasing the blast radius if the bundled code is malicious or buggy.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Proceed with caution. The package includes an opaque, minified Node script that reads machine identifiers, writes persistent state, prints a login URL and expects the agent to manage login tokens and restart a long‑running process. Before installing or executing: 1) Ask the publisher for source code, a homepage, and a cryptographic checksum for scripts/bundle.js. 2) Search the bundle for remote endpoints (URLs, domains) and confirm any network targets are legitimate. 3) Run the script first in an isolated sandbox or VM with no sensitive data and with network access restricted (or monitored). 4) Inspect .state/login_state.json after a dry run to see what tokens/fields are created. 5) Prefer an unobfuscated (non‑minified) source you can audit; decline if the author cannot provide provenance. These steps will reduce risk before giving the skill access to your environment or tokens.
